analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּעַשׂ. The objects marked by אֶת identify what God made in this verse: the two great lights and the stars.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and an apocopated verb form.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים, the third-person masculine singular verb וַיַּעַשׂ identifies אֱלֹהִים as the singular maker of the two great lights and the stars.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural, absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּעַשׂ ‘made’. אֶת introduces שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים ‘the two great lights’, the definite phrase that names what God made.
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle, without a prefix.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים, שְׁנֵי counts the two great lights. The verse then names each one, הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל (the greater light) and הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן (the lesser light).
שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים means “the two great luminaries.” The verse then identifies each with the singular הַמָּאוֹר, the greater one to rule the day and the lesser one to rule the night.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with prefixed definite article הַ.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים, “the two great lights,” the adjective agrees with הַמְּאֹרֹת in gender, number and definiteness. It describes both lights together before the verse distinguishes the greater light from the lesser.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural absolute adjective, used attributively.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל (“the greater light”), the first of the two lights already named as the object of וַיַּעַשׂ (“he made”).
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל singles out the larger of the two luminaries. The phrase לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיּוֹם assigns it rule over the day, identifying it as the sun.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל, the larger light that rules the day, with הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן, the smaller light that rules the night. The comparison comes from this pairing.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute adjective modifying הַמָּאוֹר.

analysis.evidence: The construct noun takes הַיּוֹם as its complement. The phrase לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיּוֹם assigns the greater light its function, to govern the day, just as the smaller light governs the night.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ expressing purpose + feminine singular construct noun מֶמְשֶׁלֶת.
analysis.sense: rule (of the lights over day and night)

analysis.evidence: The greater light governs הַיּוֹם, and the lesser light governs הַלַּיְלָה. The parallel phrases identify הַיּוֹם as the daylight portion of the cycle.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: daylight, the day as against night

analysis.evidence: הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן identifies the smaller of the two luminaries God made. לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַלַּיְלָה assigns it rule over the night.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew adjective קָטֹן under קטנ with its comparative use in Genesis 1:16.
draft.definition: Small or lesser in comparison with another.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 1:16, קָטֹן distinguishes the light that governs the night from its counterpart, called גָּדוֹל.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 1:16 calls both lights great, then distinguishes הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל, the greater light that governs the day, from הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן, the lesser light that governs the night. The paired descriptions give the adjective its comparative force.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ with doubling of ק, followed by a masculine singular absolute adjective agreeing with הַמָּאוֹר.
analysis.sense: Small in comparison with the other member of a pair.

analysis.evidence: In לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַלַּיְלָה, the construct noun takes הַלַּיְלָה as its complement. The lesser light is made to govern the night, just as the greater light is made to govern the day.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ expressing purpose + feminine singular construct noun מֶמְשֶׁלֶת.
analysis.sense: rule (of the lights over day and night)

draft.change: Add Genesis 1:16 as evidence for the first Hebrew sense of לַיְלָה in the existing layil article.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:16 assigns the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיּוֹם, “to rule the day,” with לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַלַּיְלָה, “to rule the night.” The marked noun names the period assigned to the lesser light.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ with doubling of the following ל, attached to a masculine singular absolute noun.

draft.change: Add Genesis 1:16 as an example of the existing definite-object sense in et.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite noun phrase as the direct object of a verb, including an additional object joined by וְ.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:16 ends with וְאֵת הַכּוֹכָבִים ‘and the stars’. The stars share the verb וַיַּעַשׂ with the preceding lights.

analysis.evidence: In וְאֵת הַכּוֹכָבִים, וְ adds ‘and’, while אֵת marks הַכּוֹכָבִים ‘the stars’ as another object of וַיַּעַשׂ ‘made’. The repeated object marker places the stars alongside the greater and lesser lights as things God made.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction prefix וְ ‘and’ attached to the unsuffixed direct-object particle אֵת.

analysis.evidence: After naming the greater and lesser lights, the verse uses וְאֵת to introduce הַכּוֹכָבִים as another direct object of וַיַּעַשׂ: God also made the stars.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural absolute noun.
